AUTHOR: Villon
TITLE: Toward an artificial intelligence-assisted counting of sharks on baited video
REGION: New Caledonia reefs, South Pacific (185 BRUVS stations)
SPECIES: Evaluated: Carcharhinus amblyrhynchos, C. melanopterus, Triaenodon obesus; trained on 8 shark species + 19 non-shark species
DATA: Own BRUVS footage: 185 one-hour videos (163 training / 22 testing stations); 1,366 clips of 15-20 s from training stations; 23,222 frames; 26,947 annotations
D_EV: Sec. 2.1: 'Using a 80% training/20% testing random split on videos rather than images ensured full independency between images of the training set and testing set.'
R_EV: Sec. 1.1: 'We collected one-hour baited videos (BRUVS) at 185 different stations across New-Caledonia's reefs' (all training and test data from the same survey)
C_EV: Sec. 2.2: 'we considered a predicted MaxN to be true if, for a given species, the predicted number of individuals was consistent across at least 2 consecutive frames'; 'we manually reviewed the network's annotations, making corrections where necessary'
E_EV: Sec. 3.2: 'Significant correlations existed between MaxN shark abundance automatically predicted by our deep-learning models and manually estimated by biologists (Fig. 2).'
ARCH: Faster R-CNN with NASNet backbone (TensorFlow 2 model zoo 'faster_rcnn_nas'), 1333x800 input, 200k iterations, 5-fold CV; MaxN = max per-frame count with 2-consecutive-frame consistency rule
METR: Precision, recall, F-measure per species; MaxN correlation (R), linear regression slope/intercept, MaxN accuracy; automated vs semi-automated comparison
NOTE: V: no visibility/turbidity information at all. D: both the station split (163/22 one-hour videos) and clip split are at video level and the authors explicitly justify this to avoid near-identical frames leaking (D4=Y). R: all data from one New Caledonia BRUVS survey; one-hour test videos are a harder use case but same distribution. C1=NR: no detection confidence threshold is reported anywhere. C5 coded as human verification of detections: the semi-automated workflow had biologists review all model annotations of the 5th-fold test set and the automated precision (0.76/0.58/0.23) quantifies false positives; the 2-consecutive-frame rule is an explicit FP mitigation for MaxN. Verifier may consider C5 borderline (full review rather than a sample). E: MaxN compared with biologist MaxN of the same videos (R=0.85-0.88 pooled; 0.35-0.90 per species), so E5 = same-footage human reading and E_ALL=P; no independent reference. E4=없음: recall reported but no explicit false-negative rate or size-class analysis (regression slope <1 is interpreted as missed sharks at high abundance). NCLASS=27 trained classes (3 evaluated). Data on request; no code.
